preconditions.description: Input consists of exactly two lines: the first line is the integer |s|, and the second line is the string s.
The integer |s| matches the length of the string s.
The string s consists only of lowercase Latin letters.
The length of s is between 1 and 100, inclusive.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the maximum number of characters that can be removed from s, not exceeding the original length of s.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout) <= len(s) for s in [stdin.splitlines()[1]] if len(s) == int(stdin.splitlines()[0]))
postconditions.description: The output is a feasible solution: there exists a sequence of operations that removes exactly int(stdout) characters from s, where each operation removes a character s_i if at least one of its adjacent characters is the previous letter in the Latin alphabet for s_i.

postconditions.expression: not any(int(stdout) < max_possible_removals(s) for s in [stdin.splitlines()[1]] if len(s) == int(stdin.splitlines()[0]))
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum possible number of characters that can be removed from s, where max_possible_removals(s) is the optimal solution for the given string s.
